## Executive assessment

Panda Express has a large, centrally managed technology estate, but the evidence shows substantial platform evolution over time rather than a safe basis for treating historical products as current. A 2026 Panda Restaurant Group job posting describes Panda as the largest family-owned American Chinese restaurant concept in America, with close to 2,800 locations globally. The same current recruiting corpus shows enterprise-wide systems administered across corporate and restaurant locations, including CrunchTime NetChef for inventory management. Panda's current licensing page also confirms a non-traditional licensing channel spanning airports, colleges, casinos, military venues, stadiums, hospitals, corporate campuses and similar venues.

The strongest POS evidence is historical. Panda selected Xpient IRIS POS in 2006 after testing it in more than 60 restaurants, with rollout to new restaurants and retrofit of existing stores. A separate 2006 report describes NCR RealPOS 70 terminals and peripherals going into new stores and retrofits. These reports are best reconciled as Xpient application software operating alongside NCR point-of-sale hardware, not as proof of two competing software deployments. Nation's Restaurant News independently confirmed in 2014 that Panda's Xpient POS was integrated to NovaDine's online/mobile ordering platform. No validated source in this bounded cycle identifies Panda's current 2026 POS software product.

Digital ordering has a clearer succession. NovaDine was verified as Panda's online/mobile ordering technology in 2014, integrated to Xpient and rolled across almost all of the then largely corporate-owned system. That evidence is historical only. Olo's SEC-filed S-1 subsequently listed Panda Express among Olo's quick-service customers and stated that Olo's customer relationships were for exclusive direct digital ordering with full participating-system coverage. Olo further reported that Panda Express named it "Tech Partner of the Year" for 2025. Panda's live 2026 website also serves menu assets from an `olo-images-live.imgix.net` host. Taken together, the evidence supports an active Panda/Olo technology relationship at high confidence, while the exact current Olo modules should not be guessed from that evidence.

Panda's loyalty and first-party mobile stack was materially rebuilt beginning in 2022. World Wide Technology says it partnered with Panda to reimagine the mobile app and establish the consumer loyalty program using AWS services including ECS, RDS, S3 and CloudWatch. Panda itself launched Panda Rewards nationally on May 30, 2023, with earning across its website, mobile app, restaurants and drive-thru. The current 2026 app supports dine-in, takeout, delivery, scheduled ordering, catering, rewards, QR-based identification and saved/reordered favorites.

For payments, the bounded cycle did not establish a current core card processor or acquiring platform. Panda's legal/privacy materials acknowledge third-party payment processors without naming them. Global Payments currently displays Panda Express among restaurant-chain logos on its restaurant POS page, but that page does not say Panda uses Global Payments Genius POS, nor does it establish which Global Payments payment-processing product Panda uses. Historical Xpient/Xenial corporate lineage is not sufficient to bridge that gap. Global Payments therefore remains a relationship/customer signal, not a verified current Panda POS or payments installation.

No Panda-specific KDS installation was validated. Crunchtime markets Crunchtime Kitchen/ConnectSmart Kitchen as a KDS, but the opened KDS page did not identify Panda as a Kitchen customer. Panda's own 2026 job posting specifically identifies CrunchTime NetChef as its enterprise inventory-management system, which is strong evidence for NetChef but not for Crunchtime Kitchen. Reporting Crunchtime Kitchen as Panda's KDS would therefore overstate the evidence.

Other supported relationships include Blackhawk Network for a 2020 nationwide digital-gifting rollout; Rokt for post-purchase ecommerce offers, independently described by Inc. in 2023; and third-party marketplace delivery. DoorDash explicitly identified Panda Express as a national partner in its 2019 Puerto Rico launch, while Panda's 2026 accounting job posting confirms that third-party delivery and marketplace-delivery accounting remain current business processes without naming current platforms.

## Approved options versus deployed vendors

### Verified deployed or relationship evidence

The following can be treated as supported technology relationships, subject to the temporal and scope qualifiers shown:

- Xpient IRIS — historical POS software deployment, verified in 2006 and still evidenced in 2014.
- NCR RealPOS 70 — historical POS terminal/peripheral deployment in 2006.
- NovaDine — historical enterprise online/mobile-ordering deployment in 2014.
- Olo — direct digital-ordering relationship established in SEC-filed Olo customer disclosures and relationship continuity evidenced through Panda's 2025 Tech Partner of the Year recognition; exact current modules not disclosed.
- World Wide Technology — app/loyalty engineering partner beginning in 2022.
- AWS ECS, RDS, S3 and CloudWatch — named components of the WWT/Panda digital stack.
- Panda Rewards — Panda's own current national loyalty program.
- CrunchTime NetChef — current enterprise inventory-management system.
- Blackhawk Network — verified 2020 digital-gifting deployment; 2026 status not established.
- Rokt — Panda client relationship for post-purchase ecommerce offers, with exact deployment scope undisclosed.
- DoorDash — verified regional third-party marketplace relationship in Puerto Rico in 2019; current nationwide scope not inferred.

### Options, signals and development claims that must not be promoted to installed status

No current FDD or Panda-authored approved-technology schedule was validated in this bounded cycle, so there is no defensible list of "approved franchisee options" to report.

- Global Payments / Genius: Panda is displayed as a restaurant-chain customer/logo on a current Global Payments page, but the evidence does not establish Genius as Panda's current POS or identify a specific Global Payments acquiring/payment product.
- Xenial self-order: Xenial says it developed a Panda self-order solution and showcased it in 2019; production rollout and location count are unverified.
- Crunchtime Kitchen / ConnectSmart Kitchen: Crunchtime's current KDS page was reviewed, but no Panda-specific Kitchen deployment was found. The validated Panda product is NetChef inventory management.
- Rokt via Olo: Olo's Rokt partner page names Panda Express among Rokt partners/clients, but it does not say Panda consumes Rokt through an Olo integration. That linkage must not be inferred.
- Olo Pay: no evidence reviewed in this cycle establishes Panda as an Olo Pay user.
- Current Xpient/Xenial POS: historical Xpient deployment and later vendor corporate lineage do not establish the exact current 2026 POS software.
- Current NCR hardware: the 2006 rollout is not sufficient to claim NCR hardware remains deployed in 2026.
- Current NovaDine: the 2014 installation is historical. The later Olo and WWT evidence means NovaDine should not be assumed current.
- Punchh: no authoritative source validated in this bounded cycle supports reporting Punchh as Panda's installed loyalty platform.

## Conflicts, negative findings, and limits

**Conflict group — 2006 POS nomenclature.** A March 2006 source calls Xpient IRIS the selected POS and says Panda would deploy it to new restaurants and retrofit existing stores. A May 2006 source says Panda selected NCR POS and specifies RealPOS 70 terminals, printers and cash drawers for new stores and retrofits. This is a superficial conflict in the word "POS," but the details support a software/hardware reconciliation: Xpient as the POS application and NCR as terminal/peripheral hardware. The 2014 NRN article independently naming Xpient as Panda's POS software materially strengthens that interpretation. Because neither 2006 article explicitly states the two components were paired, the reconciliation remains an evidence-based inference rather than a quoted architecture statement.

**Current POS negative finding.** No successfully reviewed 2026 source named Panda's current POS application. Global Payments' current customer/logo treatment is not product-specific. Historical Xpient, Heartland/Xenial lineage and Global Payments ownership should not be used to infer that Panda currently runs Genius, Xenial POS, or any other named successor product.

**Payments negative finding.** No current named core card processor, gateway or acquirer was verified. Panda's legal materials confirm the existence of third-party payment processors but do not identify them. Blackhawk's role is digital gifting/branded payments, not evidence of Panda's core restaurant card acquiring.

**KDS negative finding.** No Panda-specific KDS was validated. Crunchtime Kitchen cannot be reported as installed merely because Panda uses another Crunchtime product, NetChef. Likewise, Xenial's generic Kitchen Management capabilities are not evidence of Panda adoption.

**Approved-options/FDD negative finding.** No current Panda Express FDD or official approved-technology schedule was validated during the bounded cycle. Panda's current public expansion page is explicitly framed around licensing opportunities, especially non-traditional venues. This does not prove that no FDD exists anywhere or that every international arrangement has the same legal structure.

**Third-party delivery limit.** DoorDash has direct historical partner evidence, and Panda confirms third-party marketplace delivery remains an active accounting category in 2026. Panda's 2023 rewards announcement also mentions DoorDash and Grubhub as examples of third-party delivery services excluded from rewards earning. Those references do not, by themselves, establish current nationwide contractual scope for each marketplace, so no unverified Uber Eats/Grubhub installation has been promoted to the deployed-vendor list.

**Rokt limit.** Inc. independently identifies Panda as a Rokt client, but the reported engagement metric is explicitly attributed to the company. The current Olo partner-directory page is also partner/vendor evidence. The relationship is supported; the architecture and scope are not.

**Source-access limits.** Three opened candidate pages could not be fetched: NovaDine's Panda case study returned HTTP 502; Hospitality Technology's Xenial article returned HTTP 403; and QSR Magazine's Panda delivery article returned HTTP 403. Claims that depended uniquely on those inaccessible pages were excluded. NovaDine's historical relationship was retained only because the separately accessible Nation's Restaurant News article independently substantiated it.
